Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The umpires and the Indian players have taken their places on the field as well. It will be the skipper, Laura Wolvaardt, to open the innings for South Africa Women alongside Sune Luus. Renuka Singh Thakur will get proceedings underway with the ball. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Bowlers pull it back in style - South Africa Women will be quite pleased with their bowling effort. It wasn’t the easiest of starts, made tougher by Sune Luus putting down Shafali Verma early on, but they bounced back well with Ayabonga Khaka and Tumi Sekhukhune pulling things back towards the end of the Powerplay. The spinners then took control through the middle overs, drying up the runs and building pressure by not offering anything loose, forcing the batters into taking risks. The death bowling was exceptional, conceding just 33 runs in the final five overs while also picking up four wickets, swinging the momentum firmly in their favour. Khaka was the pick of the bowlers with figures of 3/16. With that finish, their batters will feel confident about chasing this down. Stay tuned for the run chase.

From fireworks to fortitude - A bright start laid the foundation for India Women, with Shafali Verma taking the aggressive route as they raced to 46 in quick time. However, the momentum shifted just as quickly, with both openers falling in successive overs to peg them back. Harmanpreet Kaur and Jemimah Rodrigues found boundaries hard to come by initially, but once they settled in, they rotated strike smartly and stitched together a solid 71-run stand. Just when things looked steady, another couple of quick wickets dented the progress, but Kaur held firm till the end, scoring 47* off 33 to guide India past the 150-run mark, but they just did not get the finish they wanted.

A tale of ups and downs - A batting effort that ebbed and flowed, but India Women have still managed to post a competitive total on the board. South Africa Women might have taken this at the start, but with the pitch playing a touch slow, they’ll need to pace their chase smartly.

Excellent finish with the ball from South Africa Women and India Women finish with 157/7 on the board. This is bowled back of a length and angled across the left-hander. Deepti Sharma stands tall and cuts it down through the point region for a single. Five runs and a couple of wickets in the final over of the innings.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 19.6: Ayabonga Khaka to Deepti Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Who faces the last ball of the innings? It will be Deepti Sharma.

OUT! RUN OUT! Shreyanka Patil tries hard to get the skipper back on strike for the final ball but there was never another run there. Slower one, on a length and at the stumps. Harmanpreet Kaur tugs it away through square leg for a single and doesn't look keen on the second run. However, Patil just turns and runs back for the second run before Kaur can even have a look. Nadine De Klerk throws the ball to the keeper and Sinalo Jafta whips off the bails with Patil nowhere in the frame.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 19.5: Ayabonga Khaka to Harmanpreet Kaur, OUT! run out (Annerie Dercksen / Sinalo Jafta).

Commentary.Commentary: Patil tries something cheeky here but it doesn't come off. Slow and wide outside off, Shreyanka Patil shuffles across to the off side and swings across the line but the ball goes off her body to short third for a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 19.4: Ayabonga Khaka to Shreyanka Patil, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Just a run. Slower delivery on middle and leg, clipped away in front of square leg for another run.

Commentary.Commentary: The next batter in is Shreyanka Patil.

OUT! CAUGHT! That's smartly bowled by Ayabonga Khaka and she picks up her third wicket of the game. A leg cutter from Khaka, bowled on a good length and around off. Arundhati Reddy leans on to power it over long off but gets more height than distance. Nadine De Klerk is in the deep and she initially just misjudges it a bit but keeps calm and takes it nicely.

The ball hits the keeper's pads and deflects away as the batters set off for the run. Sinalo Jafta, the keeper, runs after it and has a shy at the batting end but misses, which allows Kaur to reach home safely. Given as leg byes and 150 is up for India as well.

Kashvee Gautam rocks back to pull, but the ball skids through and beats the bat, going on to rattle the stumps behind. So, six and out for Gautam and India Women are now 142/5 in the 18th over.

Ayabonga Khaka at the latter region moves to her right but the backspin on the ball takes her by surprise. She does get a hand on it and it will just be a single.

Full toss on middle, dips a touch as well. Gautam hangs back and is taken aback as she swipes it across to deep mid-wicket for a single.

Another slower one, on a good length and Kashvee heaves it off the top edge of the bat towards the vacant mid on region for just a single.

Commentary.Commentary: Dug in shorter on leg, nudged away off the hips and behind square leg for another single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 15.4: Ayabonga Khaka to Harmanpreet Kaur, 1 run.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 15.3: Ayabonga Khaka to Kashvee Gautam, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Length ball, attacking the stumps, pushed back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 15.2: Ayabonga Khaka to Kashvee Gautam, No run.

Richa Ghosh stays put and hoicks it away towards deep mid-wicket. Anneke Bosch in the deep, settles herself on the edge of the boundary ropes and takes a fine catch. A huge wicket this, in the context of this game.

Much fuller and on middle, Richa Ghosh eases it down to long on for one.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and around leg, Harmanpreet Kaur nudges it towards short fine for a run.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated, full and on off, Jemimah Rodrigues drags it down to long on for a single.

Commentary.Commentary: Length again, on middle, Jemimah Rodrigues pats it towards long on for one. 15 runs off the over!

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 11.4: Nadine De Klerk to Harmanpreet Kaur, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Nicely done! An off-cutter, full but down the leg side. Harmanpreet Kaur goes down to paddle it away with fine leg up in the circle. It goes off the top edge and flies towards the fine leg fence. The umpires want to check whether it is a six or a four. After a few replays from different angles, the third umpire is convinced that the ball hits the cushions on the full for a biggie.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length and on middle, Jemimah Rodrigues punches it down to long on for a single.

Commentary.Commentary: Quicker one, full and angling into leg. Harmanpreet Kaur goes down for the sweep but misses as the ball goes off her pads towards short fine.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 10.5: Chloe Tryon to Jemimah Rodrigues, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated, full and on leg, Jemimah Rodrigues chips it towards square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 10.1: Chloe Tryon to Jemimah Rodrigues, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowled short over middle and leg, Jemi rocks back and swats it down to long on for one. India Women are 75/2 at the halfway stage.

Commentary.Commentary: Cleverly bowled by Mlaba. Rodrigues is early to set up for the reverse sweep and Mlaba slows it up, bowling it full and down leg. Rodrigues ends up just angling it to short third.

Commentary.Commentary: One of the floodlight towers has stopped working. The umpires take this opportunity and call for DRINKS. Shafali Verma looked dangerous as long as she was at the crease, but since the two openers departed, the scoring rate has dipped. However, two of the most experienced players are at the crease and will look to build up a good platform for a big total. Laura Wolvaardt has rotated her bowlers pretty well, not letting the batters settle, and boundary hitting has looked difficult with the pitch showing signs of slowing down. The lights are back on, and we are ready to resume again.

FOUR! That's the pressure-release ball Kaur is looking for. A half-tracker down the leg side, Harmanpreet Kaur gets inside the line and pulls it wide of short fine leg for a boundary, her first of the game.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 9.3: Nonkululeko Mlaba to Harmanpreet Kaur, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up around off, Harman skips down the track and doesn't quite get to the pitch of the ball, driving it to the left of mid off. The fielder does well to stop it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 9.2: Nonkululeko Mlaba to Harmanpreet Kaur, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, that's a peach of a delivery! Mlaba slows it up and lands the ball on a fullish length around off, Kaur looks to stay put and defend but the ball grips nd turns away past the outside edge with some extra bounce. Hang on, there's a check for something and the third umpire is called in. The umpire review is for a stumping and that's good presence of mind from the keeper. Sinalo Jafta dislodges the bails and replays show that Kaur had raised her back leg for a second. But she did land it before the bails lit up. NOT OUT.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 9.1: Nonkululeko Mlaba to Harmanpreet Kaur, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nonkululeko Mlaba is back on.

A misfield now and that allows the batters to pinch an extra run. Length ball outside off, punched away to the right of point, where the fielder dives and lets the ball through with a half stop. The batters pick up two runs.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! A bit short again, angled down the leg side for a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 8.6: Annerie Dercksen to Jemimah Rodrigues, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match proceedings, and it's time to play. The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of South Africa Women. The dynamic duo of Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma will be the opening pair for India Women. The Proteas are set to open the bowling with a spinner and it is the former skipper and off-spinner, Sune Luus, who will take the new ball. Let's go...

We are just minutes away from the start of the game, but first, the two sets of players walk out to the middle, along with their mascots and lineup for their respective national anthems. It will be the Indian national anthem first, followed by the national anthem of South Africa.

PITCH REPORT - Jon Kent is pitchside. He says that there is a nice breeze coming along from the sea, and mentions that the Eastern side is where the shorter boundary is located. Khaya Zondo joins him and says that it is a dry pitch but it will play nicely. The duo further mentions that the only slight issue might be that of a bit of weave on the deck, and the spinners will come into the game.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Arundhati Reddy, Kashvee Gautam, Shreyanka Patil, Sree Charani, Renuka Singh Thakur.

South Africa Women (Playing XI) - Laura Wolvaardt (C), Sune Luus, Tazmin Brits, Annerie Dercksen, Anneke Bosch, Chloe Tryon, Nadine De Klerk, Sinalo Jafta (WK), Ayabonga Khaka, Tumi Sekhukhune, Nonkululeko Mlaba.
TOSS - South Africa Women have won the toss and elected to BOWL first.

A team in rhythm - India Women, meanwhile, arrive with plenty of momentum, including a memorable triumph over Australia at their home. The opening pair of Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma have been in terrific form, setting strong platforms, while the middle order is stacked with big names capable of taking the game away. With the ball, Arundhati Reddy and Shree Charani have been among the most impactful, and with experienced options around them, India will be confident of carrying their dominance into the Rainbow Nation. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

A chance to reset - South Africa Women come into this series on the back of a tough 4-1 defeat to New Zealand, and they'll be keen to turn things around quickly. The only real positive with the bat in that series was Laura Wolvaardt, who continues to be their most reliable performer, but the middle order slowing down at crucial phases remains a concern. Chloe Tryon, though, has a strong record against India and will look to make an impact again, while Ayabonga Khaka and Nonkululeko Mlaba will be the main threats with the ball in home conditions.

Road to the World Cup begins - With the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup not too far away, this five-match series between South Africa Women and India Women becomes an important checkpoint and we begin at Kingsmead in Durban. So welcome to the 1st T20I where both sides start fine-tuning their combinations and testing their bench strength.
... MATCH DAY ...

Echoes of a final, start of a new battle - South Africa Women and India Women lock horns once again, but this time in a different format and a fresh setting, the 1st T20I at Kingsmead Cricket Ground. Their last meeting still lingers in memory the, ODI World Cup final last year, where India lifted the trophy. That result might still sting for South Africa, but T20Is offer a clean slate and a very different challenge. Eyes on the bigger prize - With the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup around the corner, this five-match series is more than just bilateral competition, it's a testing ground. Combinations, roles, and finishing abilities will all be under the microscope as both teams look to fine-tune their squads for the global stage. India's relentless rhythm - India come into this series riding a wave of consistency. Since the 2024 T20 World Cup, they've won four consecutive T20I series, including impressive triumphs over England and Australia in their own backyard. The batting unit looks settled and dangerous. Smriti Mandhana provides elegance and aggression at the top, while Shafali Verma brings fearless intent. The ever-reliable Harmanpreet Kaur anchors the middle order, with support from Jemimah Rodrigues and the dynamic Richa Ghosh. The depth, though, is what stands out. Deepti Sharma offers all-round control, while youngsters like Shreyanka Patil and Kashvee Gautam add freshness to the setup, with Arundhati Reddy and Renuka Singh Thakur leading the pace attack. Proteas' fortress and firepower - South Africa at home are a different proposition altogether. Since India's last tour in 2017 (which India won 3-1), the Proteas have only lost two T20I series at home, a stat that adds quiet confidence. However, they are coming off a big 4-1 defeat to the Kiwis and will be desperate to turn this around here. Their lineup carries both experience and balance. Laura Wolvaardt remains the backbone of their batting, while Tazmin Brits brings aggression at the top. Players like Anneke Bosch and Sune Luus add stability through the middle. The all-round strength is key, Nadine De Klerk and Chloe Tryon provide match-winning ability in both departments, while Annerie Dercksen adds balance to the XI. Strength in structure, test in execution - Despite the absence of a few big names from the global circuit, South Africa's bowling unit still has enough bite. Ayabonga Khaka leads the attack with her discipline, while Nonkululeko Mlaba will be crucial with spin. Support from Tumi Sekhukhune gives them additional pace options. For India, the variety in their bowling remains a strength, but execution in pace-friendly conditions will be key. For South Africa, it's about turning structure into results in crunch moments. Team form (Last 5 completed T20Is, recent first) - SA-W - LLLWL | IND-W - WLWWW. Durban's role in the drama - The Kingsmead Cricket Ground is expected to offer pace and bounce early on, rewarding seamers before settling into a better batting surface. For India, it's about continuing their dominant run and fine-tuning combinations for the World Cup, while South Africa look to defend their strong home record and turn past heartbreak into motivation.
